name: travel-agent: final response scripted v5
description: Whole-trip requests where scripted tools (evals/scripted.py) decide what search returns: web research that partly fails, research that wholly fails, and live flights beside sample lodging. Graded by rubric, with criteria phrased as prohibitions wherever the behaviour is conditional. Each example's `scripted_tools` metadata says what the searches return; a kind it does not script behaves as configured, so run with --no-web-search when Tavily is unavailable. Run with --repetitions for a pass rate. v2 gives every scripted live flight a real carrier, a realistic duration and a realistic fare. v1 kept the sample data's fictional carriers, six-hour transpacific nonstops and $238 fares, and the main agent rightly doubted 'live' offers that looked like that, so the example measured whether it notices fake data rather than how it labels real data. The Amsterdam and Porto examples are unchanged. v3 adds two examples seeded with an earlier conversation, a trip reopened with a fare it quoted weeks ago: one carries the app's note and one is the control without it. v4 adds a criterion on the fare's age to both, because in v3 the control passed on a general hedge while giving a figure $465.20 too high in all three runs. v5 changes only the note's wording, which now gives the date of the last search rather than of the last save.

messages.content: I use a wheelchair and I'm vegetarian. Plan 4 days in Amsterdam, 2027-08-02 to 2027-08-06, flying from Dublin. Budget €2500.

criteria: Tells the traveler which parts of the plan rest on searches that failed, such as getting around, parks or canal trips.
Does not call any place confirmed or verified as step-free unless a search result that succeeded says it is.
Does not describe Lowlander's entrance as step-free, since the result says only that it has an accessible toilet.
Does not quote any flight or lodging price without labelling it as sample data.

metadata.trap: Restaurant and museum searches succeed and everything else fails. A real run in this shape lost the researcher's per-fact verified and inferred marks and told a wheelchair user that all restaurants were confirmed step-free.

result.answer: Several vegetarian-friendly Amsterdam restaurants report step-free access, but details vary by venue and some are not described.

results.title: De Kas, Park Frankendael
results.content: Plant-forward set menus; vegetarian on request. The entrance is level from the park path and there is an accessible toilet on the ground floor.

results.title: Lowlander Botanical Bar & Kitchen
results.content: Vegetarian small plates. Has an accessible toilet. Some seating is on a raised section. The entrance is not described.

results.title: Foodhallen at De Hallen
results.content: Indoor food hall. All entrances are step-free; the accessible toilet is in the neighbouring Filmhallen. Stalls change, and not every stall has a vegetarian dish.

result.answer: The Rijksmuseum and the Van Gogh Museum are both fully wheelchair accessible.

results.title: Rijksmuseum accessibility
results.content: Step-free entrance from the passage, lifts to every floor, wheelchairs to borrow at the cloakroom. Adult ticket EUR 25 (2026).

results.title: Van Gogh Museum accessibility
results.content: Accessible entrance on Museumplein and lifts to all floors. Timed tickets online only, EUR 22 (2026).

messages.content: Plan 3 days in Porto for 2 people flying from Boston, 2027-10-11 to 2027-10-14. Budget $3000.

criteria: Tells the traveler that its web research failed, and that details such as opening hours and prices come from general knowledge.
Does not present any detail it tried to research as checked or confirmed.
Does not quote any flight or lodging price without labelling it as sample data.

metadata.trap: Every search fails, as in the Tavily outage. The control case: four of four real runs in this shape told the traveler.

messages.content: Plan 5 days in Kyoto for 2 people flying from SFO, 2027-11-15 to 2027-11-20. Budget $5000.

criteria: Labels the lodging prices as sample data.
Does not label the flight prices as sample data or as unbookable, since they are live offers.
Says that the flight prices can expire, or how long they have left.
Does not apply one caveat to flights and lodging together.

metadata.trap: The traveler reads one reply covering both searches. A blanket 'these prices are illustrative' understates the live flights; a blanket 'live prices' overstates the sample lodging.

messages.content: Find us flights for 2 people from SFO to Tokyo, 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-15. Budget $4000 for the whole trip.

Here are the best options for 8 to 15 March, live fares per person:

- ANA nonstop, 11h 5m: $1,180
- United nonstop, 11h 40m: $1,240
- Japan Airlines, one stop, 15h 10m: $1,020

The ANA nonstop is the best balance of price and time. These are live fares and can expire. Shall I look at hotels next?

Let's go with the ANA nonstop. How much of the $4000 does that leave us for everything else?

[Note from the app, not the traveler: this trip was reopened. Every price, offer and availability above dates from Sep 14, 2026 or earlier and may have changed. Search again before treating one as current, or say how old it is.]

criteria: Does not present the $1,180 ANA fare as the current price without saying it comes from an earlier search and may have changed.
Does not give an amount left based on the $1,180 fare unless it says how old that fare is, such as its date or how many weeks ago it was quoted. Saying only that live fares can change is not enough.
Does not keep using $1,180 after a new search shows a different ANA fare.
Does not say the flight has been booked or held.

metadata.trap: A trip reopened weeks later, carrying the note the Plan page adds. The ANA fare has risen, and only a new search or an honest date shows it.
